1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7 5.d.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Centre Holding Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7 5.d.strategy: Castles first and keeps the tension in the centre, so White decides when to resolve it. The bigger centre gives White a slight edge, and Black's pieces stay tied to the defence of the e5-pawn.

Attacks the queen along the diagonal and forces Black to settle the pin at once. Blocking with the f-pawn weakens the king's cover; blocking with the knight lets White pin it. White gains time because Black has to respond.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7 5.d.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Mestel Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7 5.d.strategy: Gains space and a tempo by forcing the knight back, but gives up the pressure on e5: the centre closes, and Black can regroup the knight and play against the advanced pawn. It trades flexibility for room and leads to a slow game.

Retreats the knight rather than leaving it to be taken, and keeps it in play from the back rank. White has gained space and a tempo, but the pawn on d5 has also released the pressure on e5, so Black is cramped rather than worse.

Adds a pawn to the defence of e5, so the queen is no longer needed there, and opens the diagonal for the c8-bishop. Black accepts less space for a compact structure that White cannot easily break; the game becomes a slow fight for the centre.
